decisions.reason: The inadmissible-input branch previously required global conditional positivity and neighborhood differentiability decisions with no oracle. Added total correct admissibility and exact-value oracles explicitly as primitive operations, preserving every branch, strict hypothesis and augmented system. Finite pivot selection and back substitution solve the unchanged invertible matrix.

The rejection is correct as a nonfatal title overclaim: the proof fixes a smooth bump and a sufficiently large T existentially and proves a uniform positive constant, not a numerical explicit bound. Removed explicit from the title. Also made inherited Countable Choice explicit in the Statement and Given, matching A1 and the linked normalized-kernel definition. The shell count, rapidly decaying window, q^(2s-d)=q^(2nu) scaling, trace bound and singleton case are sound.

The statement omitted the Countable Choice required by the ball-volume and linear change-of-variables interfaces. A1 stated the inherited assumption, but the unconditional exported Statement did not carry it. Added Countable Choice to the Statement and Given. Disjoint q-balls in a fixed R+1 ball give N <= (R+1)^d q^(-d); combining the separation estimate with q >= h/rho_0 gives exponent d+2nu=2s. The singleton convention and exact-arithmetic caveat are preserved.

A1 incorrectly called smoothing and Gaussian inversion choice-free while F2, the spectral Gaussian/Fubini/polar suppliers in F6, and integration by parts F7 require Countable Choice. The Statement already assumes full AC, which supplies these prerequisites; hence the density proof remains valid and this is nonfatal assumption-accounting prose. Replaced A1 with the exact inherited uses. Frequency truncation, bounded-weight smooth approximation, coordinate integration by parts and Gaussian-damped inversion establish all stated conclusions.
